To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a robot can be taught to recognize objects by active manipulation and by interacting with humans in a self-regulating manner.
a humanoid robot can learn to recognize objects through active curiosity-driven manipulation and in interaction and self-regulated collaboration with humans.

(i) a robot can learn object recognition from manipulation, (ii) a robot can interact with humans by actively requesting their help when necessary and (iii) a robot can self-regulate its requests for help by choosing an exploration strategy that is appropriate to its competence level.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a life-long learning system that can learn to recognize objects by active exploration and in interaction with humans.
a developmental approach to learning object recognition by manipulation, which is based on the cognitive development of human infants.
the integration of perception, control and learning in a cognitive architecture for humanoid robots.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

we show that a robot can autonomously learn to manipulate objects and to recognize their shapes, in interaction with humans, by choosing the adequate manipulation strategy to enhance competence development.
the robot learns to recognize objects by interacting with humans and by choosing the most profitable way of exploration.
our system is capable of autonomously learning to recognise objects through curiosity-driven interaction with the environment and with human teachers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a humanoid robot can learn to recognize objects by active manipulation and in interaction to humans by choosing the adequate interaction method.
we show that the iCub can autonomously learn to manipulate objects and to recognize them by interacting with teachers.

we have shown how the combination of curiosity-driven exploration, active perception and interactive learning with humans can lead to a system capable to learn object recognition through active manipulation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a developmental approach to perception, based on active exploration and interaction with humans, is feasible and effective in the context of a humanoid robot.

the iCub can autonomously learn how to recognize objects by manipulating them and that it can learn to recognize objects in interaction with humans by actively choosing the most profitable exploration strategy.
a cognitive architecture can be used as a tool for the development of a humanoid robot, and the cognitive architecture can also be used to learn how the robot should behave in a particular scenario.
